analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 1254-1648). The only change to this file is a documentation edit near the top: a new v0.10.1 candidate section replaces the v0.10.0 header, and head lines 11-138 are added. That head text is outside my supplied units. I saw only a truncated patch excerpt, so I could not assess the new rollout notes beyond their first lines. The base text I examined is historical release notes. It is prose and has no executable or security-control effect.

Relevant threat IDs (T-041, SEC-035) appear in the changelog as historical entries. Examples are the 30-minute SSD prefix-cache TTL, the HMAC-keyed cache names and the demand-gated writes. These match the retained T-041 description (30-minute TTL, KEK-derived HMAC lookup tags), so I found no drift between the base changelog and the canonical threat model.

The patch excerpt states that a coordinator without darkbloom-platform#411 can pass logprob requests to a 0.10.0 GLM provider. That provider fails them with a 500 generation_failure that cools every provider of the model. This is a documented operational and availability caveat about backend behavior. Backend implementation is out of scope, and the excerpt is truncated, so I raised no finding. It is a cross-version availability contract that a later pass should check against the provider code. The excerpt also says page-cache accounting can count more memory as available. That could affect load admission and the T-029 availability posture, but the code change is not in my supplied units.

No source code, authorization, encryption or attestation changes were visible. The remaining questions are about the unseen head-side changelog text and the provider code it describes: the GLM logprob groundwork, the page-cache accounting change and the libs/mlx-swift-lm bump. Those need examination in other units.
